messages:
Kai: Quick thread — proposal for per-org rate policy we can ship next quarter. Problem: noisy tenants + bursty ML workloads are causing tail latency and unfair token spend. My rough idea: default RPM/TPM + a small concurrency cap per org, with a short burst window and a soft grace for healthy apps. Example: RPM=3k, TPM=50k, concurrency=60, burst_window=10s, burst_tokens=2x. Thoughts?

Jessica: +1 on wanting a bounded concurrency cap. Couple Qs: are RPM/TPM enforced at ingress gateway or at the model worker? enforcement scope affects accuracy of headroom.

Mike: Gateway enforcement is necessary for tenant fairness. Worker-side checks help protect backend but are late for routing decisions. Also: 3k RPM might be small for enterprise batch embedding jobs. We need tiering: free/dev / standard / enterprise defaults.

Sasha: UX: console should show current effective limits (org tier + overrides) and a small simulation widget: "If I send X rps for Y min, estimated throttles". Also expose a per-route override so customers can bump concurrency for embeddings-only routes.

Kai: Agree on tiering. Proposal updated: tiers = {dev: RPM=300, TPM=6k, conc=8}, standard: {3k/50k/60}, enterprise: {30k/500k/1200}. Engineers can request temporary burst increases via support API.

Jessica: Policy enforcement model: token-bucket for RPM/TPM with refill per second, plus semaphore for concurrency. Burst behavior: allow bucket to go up to 2x for 10s (burst_window) then drain. Provide telemetry counters: throttled_count, dropped_count, burst_used, avg_wait_ms.

Mike: Important: monitoring alerts on sustained throttles (e.g., >5% requests throttled for 5m) and per-org cost impact. Also add a "grace tokens" concept for cold-starts or canary rollouts — small allowance so rollout traffic doesn't get killed immediately.

Sasha: For rollouts UX: when we change per-org defaults, show a preview timeline in console and a rollout plan (canary → orgs by usage deciles). Provide one-click revert.

infra-bot: deploy note: rate-limiter v1.2 will land in staging tomorrow, includes concurrency semaphores and burst_window logic. Please attach perf tests in #eng-runtime.

Kai: Implementation notes: prefer moving decision to a centralized fast path in the gateway. Keep enforcement cheap: atomic counters + token-bucket in fast memory; mitigate clock drift with leaky-bucket approximation. Persist counters for quota reporting but not for enforcement.

Jessica: Security/abuse: require org-level API owners to opt into higher tiers; auto-escalation should be manual with audit log. Also tie enterprise SLAs to guaranteed concurrency floor.

Mike: Small gotcha — embeddings clients often use long-lived streaming connections. Concurrency cap needs to count in-flight streaming sessions, not just request count. Watch for socket pinning behavior.

Sasha: UX follow-ups: add a per-org "why am I throttled" modal with recent sample traces and suggestions: lower batch size, enable caching, request dedicated pool.

Kai: Action items:
- Kai: write design doc with example token-bucket math and tier defaults (due EOD tomorrow).
- Jessica: draft telemetry dashboard (throttle %, burst usage, per-route) and alerts (due Wed).
- Mike: perf tests for streaming concurrency and burst patterns (due Fri).
- Sasha: mockups for console simulation + preview rollouts (due Thu).
- infra-bot: deploy staging build and post link.

Jessica: :thumbsup: sounds good. Can we also include a metric for "requests delayed vs outright throttled" so customers see if we queue vs drop?

Kai: Yes — plan is to surface delayed_count and avg_queue_ms. Queueing should be bounded and prioritized by org tier.

Mike: One more: consider per-org cost credits to allow controlled bursts above committed TPM for a fee. That simplifies enterprise conversations.

Sasha: agreed. ok folks i'll turn these into tasks in the eng-platform board.

Kai: Thanks all — will ping once the doc is up.
